claim: The governed environment. Governance mechanisms enforce engineering obligations by acting directly on observable work or through explicit models that expose richer semantics. Durable models, mechanisms, procedures, and documentation accumulate as engineering capital.

topology.description: Six-node accumulation ontology with two surfaces, not a pipeline or enclosing group.

required_terms: Governance mechanism Constraint · Sensor · Validator · Gate
Directly observable work Action · artifact · execution result Local rules can act directly
Explicit model / invariant Architecture · behavior · policy · bounds Exposes richer semantics
Engineering Capital Durable models · mechanisms · procedures · canonical documentation
bw_encoding: One 8% role marks explicit obligation/model semantics; mechanisms, work, environment and capital remain white.
redesign: One 8% role marks explicit obligation/model semantics; mechanisms, work, environment and capital remain white. Existing horizontal/vertical paths retained; no diagonal process-routing exception.
alt: Six vertically arranged concepts form an accumulation ontology. Governance mechanism points upward to engineering obligation and branches downward to directly observable work and an explicit model or invariant. The governed engineering environment below points upward to both surfaces. Engineering capital at the bottom points upward to the environment, labeled accumulates in. Obligation and explicit model use the same pale gray; all other nodes are white.

review.reference: current authored SVG (not older D2 receipts)
review.outcome: Rebuilt six-node ontology. Restored environment node, environment-to-both-surfaces arrows and capital-to-environment accumulation. Removed false enclosing-group substitution and reversed accumulation paths. Orthogonal branches preserve two mechanism surfaces.
review.strict_compile: zero warnings, overfull boxes, missing glyphs or errors
